sources.entry: Atomic operations, C++ working draft - The normative wording for every memory order, fence and read-modify-write, the text a compiler is checked against.

summary.title: 32 Concurrency support library [thread]
summary.one_liner: The C++ working draft's normative wording for std::atomic, memory_order, lock-free queries, atomic wait/notify, and fences, as a reference for what compilers must implement.
takeaways: memory_order defines release, acquire, acq_rel, seq_cst and relaxed semantics; a release store synchronizes with an acquire load that reads its value.
seq_cst operations and fences form a single total order S, but this only gives sequential consistency for data-race-free programs using exclusively seq_cst operations.
ATOMIC_*_LOCK_FREE macros report 0, 1 or 2 for never, sometimes, or always lock-free, and the result is the same for all atomic objects of a given type.
atomic wait and notify operations let a thread block until an atomic value changes, instead of polling.
The draft also specifies out-of-thin-air value restrictions with worked examples (Notes 5 and 6).
summary.summary: This page is a section of the C++ working draft (the [thread] clause, atomics part) rendered on eel.is. It lists the synopsis of the atomics library: memory_order, the ATOMIC_*_LOCK_FREE macros, std::atomic and its partial specialization for pointers, non-member atomic functions, atomic_flag, atomic_ref, and fences. It then gives the normative semantics: release/acquire synchronization, coherence ordering, the single total order for seq_cst operations, and guidance against out-of-thin-air values. The text is dense specification wording rather than a tutorial, and it is truncated partway through the atomic_ref section.
